ai_discrete_continuous_embedding.name: Embedding Discrete Decisions in Continuous Dynamics

sections.body: Mixed models couple a discrete active-inference layer that selects policies to a continuous layer that realises them: the discrete outcome supplies a prior over continuous setpoints, and the continuous layer's evidence feeds back as a likelihood for the discrete states. ai_generalized_coordinates.name: Generalized Coordinates of Motion
ai_generalized_coordinates.objective: Represent a continuous state by stacking it with its successive time-derivatives.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: Quantitative learner-facing values are claim-token backed by tested kernels: pc_posterior_estimate, pc_prior_prediction_error, pc_sensory_prediction_error.

sections.body: In continuous-time active inference a state is tracked together with its velocity, acceleration, and higher derivatives — a point in generalized coordinates of motion. Beliefs become trajectories rather than instantaneous estimates, and prediction errors are computed at each order, which is what lets a predictive-coding agent anticipate smooth dynamics instead of reacting to samples one at a time. Even at a single order the mechanism is exact for the linear-Gaussian case: descending the free energy along precision-weighted prediction errors settles the estimate at 1.33333, the analytic posterior mean, where the sensory error 0.666667 and the prior error 1.33333 balance once weighted by their precisions.

ai_multi_scale_temporal_hierarchies.name: Multi-Scale Temporal Hierarchies
ai_multi_scale_temporal_hierarchies.objective: Let slow high-level beliefs supply priors for fast low-level updates across timescales.

sections.body: Deep temporal models separate timescales: a high level that changes slowly supplies empirical priors to a faster low level, so context set higher up constrains moment-to-moment inference below. Free energy decomposes across levels and timescales, and the same minimisation that updates a fast percept also slowly revises the context that framed it — the structural basis of planning over nested horizons.

sections.body: In continuous state-spaces, gradient descent on the Laplace free energy yields prediction-error minimisation — the canonical microcircuit hypothesis. The same precision knob that enables coordination enables fragility.

col_stigmergy.objective: Explain how environmental traces externalise belief and coordinate agents.

sections.body: Stigmergy is coordination through persistent modifications of a shared environment - ant pheromone fields, wasp nest geometry - rather than direct messaging. The environment acts as an externalised, slowly-decaying belief state that every agent both reads and writes. This offloads memory and inference into the world, letting a colony aggregate evidence across time without any individual holding the global picture.

sections.body: Swarm intelligence is decentralised inference: each agent follows local update rules using only neighbour and environmental signals, yet the collective computes a coherent decision. Robustness comes from redundancy and the absence of a single point of failure; adaptability comes from the same free-energy gradient acting at every node. The design lesson is that global competence need not require global information.

fep_collective_inference.name: Coupling Generative Models Across Minds
fep_collective_inference.objective: Explain how shared observations couple individual generative models into population inference.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: If person A holds a generative model $p_A(o,s)$ and person B holds $p_B(o,s)$, then conditioning on the same observation $o$ makes their posteriors $p_A(s\mid o)$ and $p_B(s\mid o)$ estimates of the same hidden cause. Communication couples the models further: one agent's posterior can act as another's prior, and an ecosystem-level observer can pool the individual posteriors into a population-level belief over $s$. How tightly the population converges depends on the precision each agent assigns its evidence and on the diversity of their priors, so it is this coupling — not any single mind — that the information-ecosystem view actually treats as one generative model.

hier_attention_precision.name: Attention as Precision Control
hier_attention_precision.objective: Model attention as the gain (precision) applied to ascending prediction errors, selecting which errors drive belief updating.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: Within hierarchical predictive processing, attention is the optimisation of precision $\Pi^{(\ell)}$ on ascending prediction errors: high precision amplifies a channel's influence on higher-level beliefs, low precision attenuates it. Because the precision-weighted error $\Pi\,\xi$ is what updates beliefs, modulating $\Pi$ gates which sensory streams 'win' - the formal account of selective and divided attention. Precision is itself inferred (and can be set by higher levels), so attention becomes an endogenously controllable hyperparameter rather than a separate module. Mis-set precision is implicated in conditions ranging from hallucination (too-high prior precision) to autistic perception (atypical sensory precision).

hier_cortical_hierarchies.name: From Predictive Coding to Cortical Hierarchies
hier_cortical_hierarchies.objective: Map hierarchical predictive coding onto the laminar and connectional structure of cortex and its message-passing physiology.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: Hierarchical predictive coding offers a process theory for cortex: superficial pyramidal cells are proposed to encode precision-weighted prediction errors carried by feedforward connections, while deep pyramidal cells encode predictions carried by feedback connections, with the canonical microcircuit implementing the reciprocal exchange. Precision is associated with synaptic gain set by neuromodulation (e.g. dopaminergic/cholinergic), linking attention to physiology. This mapping makes the framework empirically committal - it predicts distinct spectral signatures (e.g. feedforward gamma, feedback beta) for errors versus predictions. The correspondence remains a theoretical proposal under active test, not a settled fact, and should be held as such.

hier_deep_temporal.name: Deep Temporal Models
hier_deep_temporal.objective: Represent states evolving at multiple timescales, with slow high-level states contextualising fast sequences below.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: A deep temporal model is a hierarchy in time: high levels evolve slowly and each of their states unfolds, at the level below, into an entire sequence of faster states. Formally one high-level transition spans many low-level timesteps, so a single abstract cause (e.g. a word) generates a temporally extended trajectory (its phonemes). This temporal nesting lets the agent represent long-range structure without an unmanageably long flat state space, and it provides natural boundaries for sequence segmentation. Inference alternates between fast within-sequence updates and slower across-sequence updates, mirroring the fast/slow timescale logic of perception itself.

hier_empirical_priors.name: Empirical Priors: Top-Down Predictions
hier_empirical_priors.objective: Treat a higher level's prediction as the empirical prior constraining inference at the level below.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: An empirical prior is a prior whose value is itself inferred - here, the top-down prediction $P(s^{(\ell)} \mid s^{(\ell+1)})$ supplied by the level above. Unlike a fixed prior, it is updated continuously as higher-level beliefs change, so context flows downward to shape lower-level inference. This is how hierarchical inference implements expectation effects: an ambiguous low-level signal is disambiguated by the contextual prediction descending from above. The recursive use of empirical priors at every level is what gives deep models their characteristic context-sensitivity.

hier_generative_models.name: Deep Hierarchical Generative Models
hier_generative_models.objective: Stack generative models so that the hidden states of one level generate the priors of the level below.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

sections.body: A hierarchical generative model factorises the world across levels, where the latent state at level $\ell+1$ parameterises the prior (and often the dynamics) of level $\ell$: $P(s^{(\ell)} \mid s^{(\ell+1)})$. Higher levels capture slower, more abstract or more invariant causes; lower levels capture fast, concrete sensory detail. This conditional structure lets the same observation be explained by a chain of nested causes, factorising an otherwise intractable joint into manageable conditional pieces. It is the architectural premise on which empirical priors, deep temporal models, and cortical-hierarchy analogies all rest.

hier_mixed_models.name: Mixed Continuous-Discrete (Hybrid) Models
hier_mixed_models.objective: Couple a discrete high-level model to continuous low-level dynamics through a Bayesian model-averaging interface.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: Hybrid models join a discrete active-inference model (good for policies and abstract states) on top of continuous predictive-coding dynamics (good for sensorimotor signals). The interface works by Bayesian model averaging: the discrete level posts a set of continuous hypotheses (priors over continuous causes), the continuous level evaluates each via its free energy, and the resulting evidences are passed back up as a discrete likelihood. This lets a symbolic plan set the target for a continuous controller while continuous outcomes inform discrete inference. It is the canonical scheme for grounding discrete decision-making in continuous embodiment.

hier_model_averaging_levels.name: Bayesian Model Averaging across Levels
hier_model_averaging_levels.objective: Marginalise over uncertain higher-level causes by averaging lower-level inferences weighted by higher-level posterior beliefs.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: When a higher level is itself uncertain among several causes, the level below should not commit to one top-down prediction but average over them, weighted by the higher-level posterior - Bayesian model averaging applied within the hierarchy. This yields a mixture empirical prior $\sum_k Q(s^{(\ell+1)}=k)\,P(s^{(\ell)}\mid k)$ that propagates higher-level ambiguity downward honestly rather than prematurely collapsing it. The same averaging is what couples discrete and continuous levels in hybrid models and what lets an agent hold multiple contextual hypotheses until lower-level evidence adjudicates. It is the hierarchical face of model averaging seen in flat model comparison.

hier_nested_free_energy.name: Multi-Scale / Nested Free Energy
hier_nested_free_energy.objective: View the total free energy as a sum of per-level contributions, minimised jointly across nested spatial and temporal scales.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: In a deep model the variational free energy decomposes additively over levels and timescales: each level contributes an accuracy term (its prediction error against the level below) and a complexity term (divergence of its posterior from its empirical prior from above). Minimising the total means every level simultaneously balances fitting the level beneath it against conforming to predictions from the level above. This nesting realises the free-energy principle across scales - the same objective governs a synapse, a cortical column, and a behaving agent. It also makes explicit that complexity at one level is regularised by the prior supplied by the level above, not by a hand-set penalty.

hier_prediction_error_passing.name: Prediction-Error Message Passing Across Levels
hier_prediction_error_passing.objective: Propagate precision-weighted prediction errors upward and predictions downward to perform inference over the whole hierarchy.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: Hierarchical inference is implemented by message passing: each level sends top-down predictions to the level below and returns bottom-up prediction errors to the level above. Under a Gaussian (Laplace) approximation these messages are precision-weighted prediction errors $\xi^{(\ell)} = \Pi^{(\ell)}\big(\mu^{(\ell)} - g(\mu^{(\ell+1)})\big)$, and belief updating ascends the free-energy gradient until errors are minimised across all levels simultaneously. Only the residual that a level cannot explain is forwarded upward, so well-predicted signals are 'explained away' and do not propagate. This reciprocal exchange is the computational core shared by predictive coding and discrete hierarchical active inference.

sections.body: Propagate precision-weighted prediction errors upward and predictions downward to perform inference over the whole hierarchy.

hier_sophisticated_inference.name: Sophisticated Inference over Hierarchies
hier_sophisticated_inference.objective: Plan over beliefs about future beliefs - recursive, counterfactual planning that exploits hierarchical and temporal depth.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: Sophisticated active inference computes the expected free energy of policies conditioned on the agent's own anticipated future beliefs, $G$ evaluated over $Q(s_\tau \mid \text{future observations})$, rather than over states alone. This recursion - reasoning about what one will believe after acting and observing - enables genuine information-seeking detours and contingency plans that 'naive' inference misses. In a hierarchy it lets abstract levels reason about how lower-level uncertainty will be resolved by future evidence, coupling deep temporal structure to deep epistemic planning. The cost is a deeper recursion, again controlled by horizon and pruning.

hier_temporal_depth_policies.name: Temporal Depth & Deep Policy Trees
hier_temporal_depth_policies.objective: Extend planning over multi-step policy trees whose expected free energy is evaluated to a chosen temporal horizon.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: Temporal depth in action means evaluating policies that are sequences of actions, scoring each by its cumulative expected free energy $G(\pi) = \sum_{\tau} G(\pi,\tau)$ to a planning horizon. As the horizon grows, the policy space branches into a tree whose size is exponential in depth, so deep planning demands pruning. Hierarchical and deep temporal structure tames this by letting high levels plan over abstract sub-goals while low levels fill in the details, factorising one deep tree into shallow trees per level. The horizon thus trades foresight against tractability.

im_channel_capacity.name: Shannon Channel Capacity
im_channel_capacity.objective: Define channel capacity as the maximal mutual information over input distributions.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

sections.body: A discrete memoryless channel $p(y\mid x)$ has capacity $C=\max_{p(x)} I(X;Y)$, the largest reliable rate (bits per channel use) achievable with vanishing error as block length grows. Capacity is a property of the channel alone: it is the supremum over input distributions of the mutual information, and the noisy-channel coding theorem proves rates below $C$ are achievable and rates above $C$ are not.

im_empowerment.objective: Define empowerment as the channel capacity from actions to future sensations.

sections.body: Empowerment is the channel capacity of the actuation-perception loop: $\mathfrak{E}=\max_{p(a^n)} I\big(A^n;\,S_{t+n}\big)$, the maximal mutual information an agent's action sequence can establish with its future sensory state. It measures how much potential control the agent has over its own future and is an intrinsic, reward-free drive: states with high empowerment keep options open. It reuses the capacity maximisation of im_channel_capacity with actions as the channel input.

im_fisher_information.name: Fisher Information as a Local Measure
im_fisher_information.objective: Define Fisher information and read it as the local curvature of log-likelihood.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: For a parametric family $p_\theta(x)$ the Fisher information is $\mathcal{I}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{p_\theta}\!\big[(\partial_\theta \log p_\theta(X))^2\big] = -\mathbb{E}_{p_\theta}[\partial_\theta^2 \log p_\theta(X)]$, the expected curvature of the log-likelihood. It lower-bounds estimator variance through the Cramer-Rao bound $\mathrm{Var}(\hat\theta)\ge 1/\mathcal{I}(\theta)$, so it quantifies how much a single observation locally informs $\theta$ - a local counterpart to the global Shannon measures.

im_fisher_kl.name: Fisher Information from KL Curvature
im_fisher_kl.objective: Derive Fisher information as the second-order Taylor term of a local KL divergence.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

prerequisites.name: Fisher Information as a Local Measure

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: Expanding the KL divergence between nearby members of a family to second order gives $D_{KL}\!\big(p_\theta \,\|\, p_{\theta+\delta}\big) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\delta^\top \mathcal{I}(\theta)\,\delta + O(\|\delta\|^3)$, because the zeroth and first-order terms vanish. Thus Fisher information is the Hessian of KL at $\delta=0$ and the metric tensor of the Fisher-Rao information geometry; KL behaves locally like a (non-symmetric) squared distance whose quadratic form is $\mathcal{I}$.

im_information_bottleneck.name: The Information Bottleneck
im_information_bottleneck.objective: Formulate the optimal trade-off between compression and relevance.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: The information bottleneck seeks a representation $T$ of $X$ that compresses $X$ while preserving information about a target $Y$, minimising $\mathcal{L}=I(X;T)-\beta\,I(T;Y)$ over stochastic encoders $p(t\mid x)$. The Lagrange multiplier $\beta$ sweeps the relevant compression frontier; the data-processing inequality guarantees $I(T;Y)\le I(X;Y)$, so no representation can be more informative about $Y$ than the raw data. It formalises 'keep only the bits of $X$ that matter for $Y$.'

sections.body: Formulate the optimal trade-off between compression and relevance.

im_landauer.name: Thermodynamic Cost of Information
im_landauer.objective: Connect Landauer's bound to free energy and the cost of erasing information.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

sections.body: Landauer's principle sets the minimal thermodynamic cost of irreversibly erasing one bit at temperature $T$ to $k_B T \ln 2$ of dissipated heat, tying information directly to thermodynamics. In the variational free-energy view, free energy is measured in the same units as entropy/information (with $k_B T$ as the conversion factor), so minimising variational free energy is simultaneously a statistical and a thermodynamic optimisation. This closes the loop between Shannon information and physical work that the free-energy principle exploits.

im_predictive_information.name: Predictive Information
im_predictive_information.objective: Define predictive information as the mutual information between past and future.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: The predictive information of a stationary process is $I_{\text{pred}}=I\big(X_{\text{past}};\,X_{\text{future}}\big)$, the mutual information between the entire past and the entire future. It equals the sub-extensive part of the block entropy $H(T)$ - the amount by which $H(T)$ grows sublinearly - and upper-bounds how much any model can predict. It is a complexity measure: structureless (i.i.d.) and perfectly periodic signals both carry little predictive information, while rich generative structure carries a lot.

im_rate_distortion.name: Rate-Distortion Theory
im_rate_distortion.objective: Characterise the minimal description rate for a tolerated reconstruction distortion.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: Lossy compression is governed by the rate-distortion function $R(D)=\min_{p(\hat{x}\mid x):\,\mathbb{E}[d(X,\hat{X})]\le D} I(X;\hat{X})$, the fewest bits per symbol needed to reconstruct $X$ as $\hat{X}$ within average distortion $D$. $R(D)$ is convex and non-increasing: tolerating more distortion buys fewer required bits, and $R(0)=H(X)$ for a discrete lossless source. This is the dual of channel capacity and frames perception as lossy coding of sensory causes.

im_total_correlation.name: Multi-Information & Total Correlation
im_total_correlation.objective: Quantify the total statistical dependence among many variables.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

sections.body: Total correlation (multi-information) generalises mutual information to $n$ variables: $C(X_1,\dots,X_n)=\sum_i H(X_i) - H(X_1,\dots,X_n) = D_{KL}\!\big(p(x_1,\dots,x_n)\,\|\,\textstyle\prod_i p(x_i)\big)$. It is the KL divergence from the joint to the product of marginals, is zero exactly when all variables are mutually independent, and measures the redundancy a factorised (mean-field) model would discard.

im_transfer_entropy.name: Transfer Entropy & Directed Information Flow
im_transfer_entropy.objective: Measure directed, dynamical information transfer between coupled processes.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

sections.body: Transfer entropy from process $Y$ to process $X$ is the conditional mutual information $T_{Y\to X}=I\big(X_{t+1};\,Y_t^{(k)} \mid X_t^{(k)}\big)$: the reduction in uncertainty about $X$'s next state contributed by $Y$'s past beyond $X$'s own past. Unlike mutual information it is directional ($T_{Y\to X}\ne T_{X\to Y}$ in general) and is a model-free, non-linear analogue of Granger causality, making it the standard measure of coupling in self-organising and neural systems.

im_typical_set.objective: State the asymptotic equipartition property and characterise the typical set.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: For an i.i.d.\ source $X_1,\dots,X_n\sim p$, the AEP gives $-\tfrac{1}{n}\log p(X_1,\dots,X_n)\to H(X)$ in probability, so almost all probability mass concentrates on the typical set $A_\epsilon^{(n)}$ of roughly $2^{nH(X)}$ near-equiprobable sequences. The remaining exponentially many sequences are individually so improbable that they carry vanishing total mass, which is why $H(X)$ is the per-symbol description cost in the limit.

sections.body: Amortised inference trains a recognition network $q_\phi(s\mid o)$ - shared across all observations - to output approximate-posterior parameters in a single forward pass, instead of running an optimisation loop per datum. The network is fit by maximising the ELBO (minimising free energy) averaged over data, trading an up-front training cost and a fixed amortisation gap for $O(1)$ inference at deployment. This is the inference engine of variational autoencoders and scalable deep active-inference agents.

sections.body: Profiling attributes runtime to the actual hot paths - likelihood evaluation, the predict step, or the policy search - rather than to assumed bottlenecks, and benchmarking measures wall-clock against problem size to confirm the empirical scaling curve. sections.body: The decisive test of a generative model is a round trip: sample latent causes from a known ground truth, generate observations through the model, run inference, and confirm the posterior recovers the planted causes within a calibrated tolerance. Following a real-data discipline, the test exercises the real sampling, inference, and convergence (impl_gradient_checking, impl_reproducibility) end-to-end rather than replacing them - a green test that never runs the actual update is worthless. Posterior calibration checks (coverage of credible intervals) turn 'it ran' into 'it is correct.'

impl_gradient_checking.name: Gradient Checking & Analytic Verification
impl_gradient_checking.objective: Verify analytic gradients against finite-difference numerical estimates.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: An analytic gradient implementation is checked against the central finite difference $\partial_\theta F \approx \big(F(\theta+\epsilon)-F(\theta-\epsilon)\big)/(2\epsilon)$, with agreement to a small relative tolerance confirming correctness. The central scheme has $O(\epsilon^2)$ truncation error, so $\epsilon$ must be small enough to be accurate yet large enough to avoid floating-point cancellation. This numeric-vs-analytic check is the standard guard against silent gradient bugs in any free-energy minimiser.

impl_logsumexp.name: The Logsumexp Trick
impl_logsumexp.objective: Stabilise softmax and log-normaliser computations against overflow and underflow.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: Computing $\log\sum_i e^{x_i}$ or a softmax directly overflows for large $x_i$ and underflows for very negative ones. The logsumexp identity $\log\sum_i e^{x_i} = x^\* + \log\sum_i e^{x_i - x^\*}$ with $x^\*=\max_i x_i$ shifts the largest exponent to zero, guaranteeing at least one well-scaled term and no overflow. Every numerically robust softmax, EFE-to-policy mapping, and log-partition evaluation in an active-inference implementation relies on this stabilisation.

impl_message_passing.name: Message-Passing Implementation
impl_message_passing.objective: Implement marginal inference as local message updates on a factor graph.

sections.body: On a factor graph, belief propagation computes marginals by passing messages $\mu_{f\to x}$ and $\mu_{x\to f}$ that are products of incoming messages times local factors, with marginals recovered as the normalised product of all messages into a variable. Implemented in log-space (using impl_logsumexp) the products become sums, and on a tree the schedule converges exactly in two sweeps; loopy graphs iterate to a fixed point that approximates the marginals.

impl_monte_carlo.name: Monte-Carlo Estimators
impl_monte_carlo.objective: Estimate intractable expectations in inference by sampling.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: When an expectation $\mathbb{E}_{q}[f(s)]$ has no closed form, a Monte-Carlo estimator $\hat{\mu}=\tfrac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N f(s^{(i)})$, $s^{(i)}\sim q$, is unbiased with standard error shrinking as $O(1/\sqrt{N})$. The reparameterisation trick rewrites $s=g(\epsilon,\phi)$ so gradients pass through the sampler, enabling stochastic gradients of the free energy. The error rate is dimension-independent, which is exactly why sampling scales to high-dimensional latent spaces where quadrature fails.

impl_particle_filter.name: Particle Filtering for State Estimation
impl_particle_filter.objective: Implement sequential Monte-Carlo state estimation with resampling.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

sections.body: A particle filter represents the filtering posterior $p(s_t\mid o_{1:t})$ by weighted samples: each particle is propagated through the transition model, reweighted by the observation likelihood $w^{(i)} \propto p(o_t\mid s^{(i)}_t)$, and the set is resampled when the effective sample size collapses. It performs the same recursive predict-update as exact filtering (ai_state_estimation) but for non-linear, non-Gaussian models where closed-form belief updates are unavailable; resampling is what prevents weight degeneracy from killing the estimate.

impl_scaling_tradeoffs.name: Scaling Trade-offs & Factorisation
impl_scaling_tradeoffs.objective: Reason about state-space explosion and the factorisation that tames it.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: A joint state of $K$ factors each with $n$ levels has $n^K$ configurations, so exact inference is exponential in the number of factors - the state-space explosion. Modelling the generative model as a product of conditionally independent factors and using a mean-field posterior turns $n^K$ into roughly $K$ tensors of size $n$, trading exactness for tractability. The art is choosing a factorisation whose discarded dependencies (measured by total correlation) are small enough that the approximation stays faithful.

sections.body: Gradient-based variational inference parameterises an approximate posterior $q_\phi$ and descends the variational free energy $F(\phi)=\mathbb{E}_{q_\phi}[\log q_\phi(s)-\log p(o,s)]$ by automatic differentiation, updating $\phi \leftarrow \phi - \eta\,\nabla_\phi F$. Because $F$ upper-bounds surprise, each well-tuned step lowers the bound monotonically - the same descent illustrated numerically from 3.11735 nats down to 2.82346 nats. Implementation hinges on a differentiable $F$, a stable learning rate $\eta$, and a convergence criterion on $\Delta F$.

learn_active_learning.name: Active Learning vs Active Inference
learn_active_learning.objective: Distinguish acting to reduce parameter uncertainty (active learning) from acting to reduce state uncertainty and secure preferences (active inference).

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

sections.body: Active inference selects policies that minimise expected free energy, balancing state-epistemic value, parameter-epistemic value (novelty), and pragmatic value. \emph{Active learning} is the special emphasis on the novelty term: deliberately sampling observations expected to most sharpen the model parameters, even at some pragmatic cost. The two are not opposed but nested - active learning is active inference whose dominant drive is parameter information gain rather than goal attainment. A mature agent modulates the relative weight of novelty so that early in life it explores to build a good model and later exploits it to satisfy preferences.

learn_bayesian_model_reduction.name: Bayesian Model Reduction (Pruning)
learn_bayesian_model_reduction.objective: Prune redundant parameters offline by comparing the free energy of a full model against reduced priors, keeping only structure that earns its complexity.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

sections.body: Bayesian model reduction (BMR) evaluates, post hoc, whether a simpler prior would have yielded greater model evidence given the already-computed posterior. Because the posterior under a reduced prior can be obtained analytically from the full posterior and the two priors, BMR scores many candidate simplifications cheaply without re-fitting. Pruning a parameter (e.g. zeroing a Dirichlet count) is accepted when it increases the free-energy bound on log evidence, removing complexity that did not pay for itself. In active inference BMR is the mechanism behind sleep-like consolidation and the discovery of sparse, generalisable models.

learn_dirichlet_params.name: Dirichlet Priors over Model Parameters
learn_dirichlet_params.objective: Place Dirichlet priors over the columns of the categorical model matrices so that parameters themselves become random variables to be inferred.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

sections.body: In discrete active inference the generative model is parameterised by categorical distributions (the columns of $A$, $B$, $D$, $E$). Because the Dirichlet is conjugate to the categorical, a Dirichlet prior $\mathrm{Dir}(\mathbf{a})$ over each column makes the parameters latent variables whose posterior remains Dirichlet after observing data. The concentration vector $\mathbf{a}$ acts as a vector of pseudo-counts: its sum encodes confidence and its normalisation encodes the expected categorical. This is the formal bridge that lets an agent treat \emph{learning} as Bayesian belief updating over $\theta$ rather than over hidden states alone.

learn_habits_E.name: Learning Habits E over Policies
learn_habits_E.objective: Accumulate Dirichlet counts over selected policies to form a habit prior E that biases future policy selection.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: The habit vector $E$ is a prior over policies that is added to the expected-free-energy term in the policy posterior $\pi \propto \sigma(\ln E - \gamma\, G)$. Learning $E$ increments its Dirichlet concentration toward policies that were actually enacted, $\mathbf{e} \leftarrow \mathbf{e} + \eta\, \pi$, so frequently chosen behaviours become cheaper to repeat. This implements model-free habit formation layered on top of model-based planning: habits amortise the cost of deliberation but can entrench suboptimal routines if the environment shifts. The balance between $\ln E$ and $-\gamma G$ is therefore the formal expression of the habit-versus-deliberation trade-off.

learn_likelihood_A.name: Learning the Likelihood A by Concentration Counts
learn_likelihood_A.objective: Update the Dirichlet concentration parameters of the likelihood matrix A by accumulating expected state-observation co-occurrences.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: Learning $A$ means updating its Dirichlet concentrations $\mathbf{a}$ rather than a point estimate. After each timestep the agent adds the outer product of the posterior over states and the observed outcome, $\mathbf{a} \leftarrow \mathbf{a} + \eta\, \mathbf{o}\,\mathbf{s}_\pi^{\top}$, so that columns accrue pseudo-counts for the states believed to have generated each outcome. The expected likelihood used in inference is the row-normalised concentration, and the implicit logarithm is the digamma-corrected expectation $\psi(a_{ij}) - \psi(\sum_i a_{ij})$. Because updates are weighted by the recognition posterior, learning and perception are coupled: better state inference yields sharper likelihood learning.

learn_model_selection_averaging.name: Bayesian Model Selection & Averaging
learn_model_selection_averaging.objective: Choose among or average over competing generative models using their (variational) model evidence as weights.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

provenance.summary: This lesson record contains no kernel claim token; any quantitative examples must still enter through the provenance registry before export.

sections.body: When several candidate models are entertained, Bayesian model selection compares their log evidences (approximated by the negative free energy) and Bayesian model averaging combines their predictions weighted by posterior model probability $P(m\mid o) \propto P(o\mid m)P(m)$. Selection commits to the single best model and is appropriate when one structure clearly dominates; averaging hedges across models and is preferred under genuine structural uncertainty. Both rest on the variational free energy as a tractable proxy for log evidence, so the same quantity that drives perception and action also adjudicates between whole models.

learn_novelty_term.name: Novelty: Parameter Epistemic Value
learn_novelty_term.objective: Add a novelty term to the expected free energy that values observations expected to reduce uncertainty about model parameters.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

sections.body: Beyond state-epistemic value (resolving uncertainty about hidden states), an agent can value resolving uncertainty about its \emph{parameters} - the novelty term. Formally it is the expected information gain over the Dirichlet parameters, $\mathbb{E}_{Q(o,s|\pi)}\big[ \mathrm{KL}[\, Q(\theta\mid o,s) \,\|\, Q(\theta) \,]\big]$, which scores policies by how much they are expected to sharpen $A$ (or $B$). Novelty is largest where concentration counts are low, so the agent is drawn to under-sampled state-observation pairings. This is the active-inference formalisation of curiosity directed at the model itself rather than its current state.

sections.body: The vector $D$ encodes the prior over the hidden state at the first timestep of an episode. Learning it adds the inferred initial-state posterior to its Dirichlet concentration after each episode, $\mathbf{d} \leftarrow \mathbf{d} + \eta\, \mathbf{s}_{1}$, so that recurring starting configurations become more probable a priori. Over many episodes this lets the agent internalise the base rates of its environment's starting conditions, sharpening early-trial inference. Unlike $A$ and $B$, $D$ is updated once per episode rather than per timestep.

learn_structure_learning.name: Structure Learning: Discovering Model Form
learn_structure_learning.objective: Expand the generative model by adding hidden states or factors when new data are better explained by extra structure than by existing parameters.

sections.body: Whereas parameter learning fits a fixed model form, structure learning changes the form itself - adding hidden-state levels, new factors, or new outcome modalities. A common scheme grows the model by introducing a candidate new state whenever current explanations are surprising, then uses Bayesian model reduction to retain the addition only if it raises model evidence. This expand-then-reduce loop balances the pressure to fit data against the complexity cost in free energy. It lets an agent move from a misspecified model toward one whose latent dimensionality matches the world's.

learn_timescales.objective: Separate the fast timescale of state inference from the slow timescale of parameter learning to keep learning stable.

sections.body: Active inference operates on (at least) two timescales: states $s$ are inferred within a trial (fast), while parameters $\theta$ are updated across trials (slow). This separation arises naturally because the Dirichlet posterior over $\theta$ integrates evidence pooled over many fast-scale inferences, with a learning rate $\eta < 1$ damping each contribution. Keeping parameters quasi-stationary relative to states is what makes the variational scheme well-posed: if parameters changed as fast as states, the recognition density would chase a moving target. The regime can shift - for instance under a precision change such as 0.95 - but the timescale ordering is the default that stabilises learning.

learn_transition_B.objective: Accumulate Dirichlet counts over state transitions, conditioned on the action taken, to learn the controllable dynamics B.

sections.body: The transition tensor $B^{(u)}$ holds, for each action $u$, the categorical probability of moving from state $s_t$ to $s_{t+1}$. Learning it updates the Dirichlet concentrations $\mathbf{b}$ with the expected transition co-occurrence $\mathbf{b}^{(u)} \leftarrow \mathbf{b}^{(u)} + \eta\, \mathbf{s}_{t+1}\,\mathbf{s}_{t}^{\top}$ for the action actually executed. Because transitions are action-conditioned, credit is assigned only to the slice corresponding to the chosen $u$, so an agent must act diversely to learn the full controllable dynamics. This is what allows an agent to discover the consequences of its own actions, not merely passive correlations.

mp_belief_propagation.name: Belief Propagation on Trees
mp_belief_propagation.objective: Schedule sum-product messages to obtain every marginal in two sweeps.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

sections.body: Belief propagation is sum-product organised as a leaf-to-root then root-to-leaf sweep, so a single pass in each direction yields every variable's marginal. The belief at a node is its local evidence times the product of stabilised incoming messages, which is why the schedule terminates exactly on an acyclic graph. On a worked three-node sticky chain, a single informative reading at the middle node (posterior 0.9) propagates outward and lifts each unobserved neighbour to 0.74, a smoothing lift of 0.24 above an even prior — and these marginals match a brute-force enumeration of the full joint exactly.

sections.body: Sum-product computes a variable's marginal as the product of incoming messages from its neighbouring factors, where each factor message sums out the other variables it touches. sections.body: Variational message passing recasts mean-field coordinate ascent as messages: each factor sends expected sufficient statistics to its neighbours, and a variable updates its approximate posterior from the messages it receives. pex_explore_exploit_frontier.name: The Exploration–Exploitation Frontier
pex_explore_exploit_frontier.objective: Trace how the epistemic and pragmatic terms of expected free energy trade off.

sections.body: Expected free energy already contains both an epistemic term that rewards uncertainty-reducing actions and a pragmatic term that rewards preferred outcomes, so an active-inference agent does not need a bolt-on exploration heuristic. The balance shifts with residual uncertainty: when the world is ambiguous the epistemic term dominates and the agent gathers information, and as uncertainty resolves the pragmatic term takes over and the agent pursues its goals.

sections.body: The guidance view decomposes the pragmatic part of expected free energy into a risk term, the divergence between predicted and preferred outcomes, and an ambiguity term, the expected uncertainty of the likelihood. sections.body: Precision is the confidence the agent assigns to a signal: high precision sharpens a distribution and lets it dominate an update, low precision flattens it and defers to other evidence. The same construct appears as sensory-precision weighting of prediction errors and as the policy precision that sharpens action selection, which is why precision, not a new mechanism each time, unifies attention and decision confidence.

pex_rate_distortion_efe.name: Rate-Distortion and the Epistemic-Pragmatic Trade-Off
pex_rate_distortion_efe.objective: Read expected free energy as a rate-distortion trade-off between information and value.

officialSkillTree.routePolicy: Direct SkillTree skill-detail routes are intentionally not used for Learn actions; local validation found that subject and quiz handoff routes are the stable official SkillTree surfaces for this dashboard.

sections.body: Rate-distortion theory asks for the least information an agent must keep to hold expected distortion below a bound; expected free energy makes the mirror trade-off, balancing the epistemic value of an observation against the pragmatic value of a preferred outcome. Both say a bounded agent should pay for information only to the extent it buys reduced cost, which is why precision behaves like the slope that sets the exchange rate between bits gathered and value pursued.

sections.body: Bayesian model reduction evaluates how the free energy of an already-fitted model would change under a simpler (more precise or zeroed) prior, without re-fitting. Because the likelihood is unchanged, the evidence difference is a closed-form function of the posterior and the two priors, so many candidate reductions can be scored cheaply to prune redundant parameters and recover a sparser model.

sections.body: A mean-field posterior factorises completely and so cannot represent correlations between latent variables; a structured (or marginal) approximation keeps chosen dependency edges, reducing the bound gap where those correlations matter at the cost of more expensive updates. Choosing the factorisation is itself a modelling decision about which posterior couplings are worth paying for.
